# Exact H height identities, the degree lift, and an actual-menu compensation obstruction

This note keeps the actual projective energy normalizer and the actual
cap-menu covariance coefficients. It proves a weaker height payment with
the exact H buffer factor, then shows that normalizing the positive
source-plus-covariance density does NOT restore Gamma_d, even for a common-
budget minimizing menu of an ordinary triangle. The latter example is an
actual cap minimum, not an asserted global body minimum.

## 1. Exact source identities

Let K be a positive d-dimensional convex body, y interior, r=X-y,
N=d+1, and let P(X)=1+a.r be its attained energy normalizer:

    E=integral_K P^(-N), V=|K|,
    integral_K r P^(-N-1)=0.

The last equation implies integral_K P^(-N-1)=E. Write n for the unit
outward normal and h_y(n)=r.n on the boundary. The divergence theorem gives

    integral_boundary n P^(-N) = -N a E,
    integral_boundary r tensor n P^(-N) = E I.        (1)

For example, the (i,j) matrix entry is the integral of
delta_ij P^(-N)-N r_i a_j P^(-N-1), so the energy first-order equation
removes the second term. The actual H own response density is

    q_H=P^(-N)/(N E)+1/(d N V).

Consequently

    integral_boundary n q_H=-a,
    integral_boundary r tensor n q_H=I/d,
    integral_boundary h_y(n) q_H=1.                   (2)

Define the following probability measures on the boundary:

    nu_E=h_y P^(-N) dS/(dE),
    nu_V=h_y dS/(dV),
    nu_C=h_y P^(-d) dS/(dE),
    nu_H=h_y q_H dS=(d/N)nu_E+(1/N)nu_V.

Here nu_C is the projective cone probability. Exactly

    nu_C=P nu_E,       integral P dnu_E=1.             (3)

Thus the conversion from energy to cone credit multiplies by h_y P;
the extra reciprocal degree must not be silently retained after this step.

## 2. Projective expression and exact weaker payment

Put D=T_a(K-y), T_a(r)=r/(1+a.r). Then |D|=E and the centroid of D is0.
For xi in D put L(xi)=1-a.xi=1/P(r) and c=E/V. Let nu_D denote the
ordinary cone probability of D. The exact pushforwards are

    nu_C -> nu_D,
    nu_E -> L nu_D,
    nu_V -> c L^(-d) nu_D,
    nu_H -> [d L+c L^(-d)]/(d+1) nu_D.                (4)

The cone Jacobian supplies the first identity; (3) supplies the second;
the inverse projective cone Jacobian supplies the third. Weighted AM-GM
now gives the pointwise lower bound

    [d L+c L^(-d)]/(d+1) >= c^(1/(d+1)).

Every halfspace through y maps to a halfspace through0. Ordinary
Grunbaum in D therefore proves the exact useful estimate

    nu_H(H) >= Gamma_d (E/V)^(1/(d+1)).                (5)

In the mixed H notation of the companion response note, the factor is

    (E/V)^(1/(d+1)) = f_H(Y)/(V/M)^(1/d).

It is the actual buffer factor, and need not equal1.

## 3. The extra-degree facet lift is real but its center is different

Let F have dimension m=d-1, let tau be nonnegative and concave on its
positive convex support, and let P(x)=b+a_T.x>0 with b>0 in the chosen
facet coordinates. The density g=tau P^(-d-1) has convex inverse d-th
root. Indeed P^((d+1)/d) tau^(-1/d) is the perspective of the convex
power s -> s^((d+1)/d). This is precisely the Ball exponent m+1=d.

There is also an explicit d-dimensional convex lift

    L_F={(x,t): x in support(tau), 0<=t<=tau(x)}.

The projective map (x,t)->(x,t)/P(x) has Jacobian b P^(-d-1), so its
uniform volume is b integral_F tau P^(-d-1). Vertical facet halfspaces
map to ordinary halfspaces. Pulling its centroid's x coordinate BACK to
F gives the escort center

    x_* = [integral x tau P^(-d-2)]/[integral tau P^(-d-2)].       (6)

To verify the denominator, if A=integral tau P^(-d-1), B=integral
x tau P^(-d-2), C=integral tau P^(-d-2), then A=bC+a_T.B.
The projected centroid is B/A and its inverse projective coordinate is
bB/(A-a_T.B)=B/C. The actual section center integral x tau/integral tau
does not determine (6). This is an ordinary facet lift; it does not
preserve mixed lattice labels or glue different facets.

Nor can one apply the same inverse-power theorem directly to the FULL H
density. If A0=1/((d+1)E), B0=1/(d(d+1)V), then the sign of

    d^2/dt^2 (A0 t^(-d-1)+B0)^(-1/beta)

is the sign of

    (((d+1)/beta)-1) A0 - (d+2) B0 t^(d+1).

For beta=d it is nonnegative exactly when

    t^(d+1) <= V/((d+2)E).                             (7)

The additional own-volume term can therefore destroy the favorable
inverse-power convexity, including at arbitrarily small nonconstant P
perturbations of a centroid configuration.

## 4. An exact noncentroid source-height obstruction (scope only)

Let D=conv{(2,-1),(-1,2),(-1,-1)}, a=(1/4,0), and K=T_(-a)(D).
Thus K has vertices (4,-2),(-4/5,8/5),(-4/5,-4/5), E=9/2, V=144/25,
y=0, and P=1+X1/4. D has centroid0, certifying the attained optimizer.
For H0={X1>=0}, H1={X2>=0}, H2={-X1-X2>=0}, direct edge flux gives

                 H0          H1=H2
    nu_C         4/9          4/9
    nu_E         1/3          1/2
    nu_V         25/36        8/27
    nu_H         49/108       35/81.

In particular nu_H(H1)<Gamma_2. These raw cap volumes are unequal, so
this example only refutes an individual source-height claim. It is NOT a
critical common-budget menu and is not used for the stronger result below.

## 5. Actual centered simplex menu: covariance makes the normalized claim fail

Use K=D above, y=0, d=2, n=0, M=V=E=9/2 and P=1. Then

    Sigma=[[1/2,-1/4],[-1/4,1/2]],
    u0=sqrt(2)(1,0), u1=sqrt(2)(0,1), u2=sqrt(2)(-1,-1),
    Gamma(uj)=1, rho_j=1/3, sum rho_j uj=0.

The three through-centroid caps H_j all have raw mass (4/9)V and are
actual minimizing caps at the unique ordinary deepest point. Define the
ACTUAL menu quadratic

    Q_rho(X)=sum rho_j(uj.X)^2=(4/3)(X1^2+X1 X2+X2^2).

It has volume mean1. With nu_V=h_0 dS/(2V), homogeneous divergence gives

    integral Q_rho dnu_V=2.

On each of the three edges parametrized from one vertex to another,

    Q_rho(t)=12t^2-12t+4,    dnu_V=dt/3.

Each H_j consists of the last two-thirds of two incident edges, whence

    nu_V(H_j)=4/9,
    integral_(H_j) Q_rho dnu_V
       =(2/3) integral_(1/3)^1 (12t^2-12t+4)dt=64/81.  (8)

Since q_H=1/(2V), the positive source-plus-covariance height measure per
unit source coefficient is

    h_0 [q_H+Q_rho/(2V)]dS=(1+Q_rho)nu_V.

Its total is3 but every ACTUAL critical cap has normalized mass

    (4/9+64/81)/3=100/243 < 4/9=Gamma_2.               (9)

More generally replacing Q_rho by t Q_rho gives

    [4/9+t(64/81)]/[1+2t] < 4/9 for every t>0.        (10)

Thus even where the buffer factor c^(1/3) already equals1, the positive
menu covariance does not obey a universal normalized Gamma payment.

## 6. The obstruction persists for an actual positive-width common-budget menu

This section uses the outward uniform kernel from
`candidate 0fa64553cd01d7ae`.
Take epsilon>0 and h>0 small. At the centroid f_H=1, so the buffer is
b=epsilon. The simplex's affine permutation group preserves the covariance
normalization, H buffer, and the smoothing. Strict H concavity makes the
deepest mark unique; convexity and symmetry of deepest superlevels then
force it to be0.

The three canonical normals remain actual global minimizing normals for
all sufficiently small epsilon,h. Here is an explicit check. Near the first
normal write n=(1,t), G(t)=sqrt((1-t+t^2)/2). A cap at threshold -q G(t)
isolates the first vertex when q and |t| are small, and its area fraction is

    F_q(t)=[2-t+q G(t)]^2/[9(1-t)].                   (11)

The smoothed cap is the average of F_q over q in [epsilon,epsilon+h].
At t=0, G'=-G/2, so F_q'(0)=0 for EVERY q. At q=0,

    F_0(t)=4/9+t^2/[9(1-t)], F_0''(0)=2/9>0.

Hence a fixed small neighborhood has F_q''>0 uniformly for sufficiently
small q, and its only minimum is t=0. The other two normal neighborhoods
follow by affine permutations. At q=0 the only global minima are these
three directions: an isolating cap has centroid mass (a+b)^2/(9ab)>=4/9,
with equality a=b, while a cap containing two vertices has complementary
isolating mass at most1/2 and hence mass at least1/2. Here a,b are the two
positive vertex-value gaps; the condition that the other two vertices lie
strictly below0 gives 1/2<=a/b<=2 and the complementary isolating mass is
at most1/2. Endpoints follow by continuity. Compactness of the covariance
unit circle gives a strict gap away from the three neighborhoods. Uniform
O(epsilon+h) cap convergence retains that gap. This proves the assertion.

The common raw smoothed budget is explicitly

    beta_(epsilon,h)
      =[4+2sqrt(2)(epsilon+h/2)
                        +(epsilon^2+epsilon h+h^2/3)/2]/9.      (12)

The three positive S_j are equal to S and the three A_j equal A<=0.
For this one actual source group, lambda=1, B=1/S, kappa=S,
e=S epsilon, omega_j=1/3. Therefore the ACTUAL covariance coefficients
are exactly

    e rho_j-omega_j A=(S epsilon-A)/3,
    t_h=1-A/(S epsilon) in [1,1+h/epsilon].             (13)

Consequently the actual positive source-plus-covariance height measure
per unit e is precisely (1+t_h Q_rho)nu_V. If h=o(epsilon) and epsilon
decreases to0, t_h->1 and the boundary kernel of every selected actual cap
converges nu_V-almost everywhere to 1_(H_j). Bounded convergence and (8)
give the normalized captured fraction ->100/243. Thus for ALL sufficiently
small parameters along, for example, h=epsilon^2, this actual positive-
width common-budget minimizing menu still violates normalized Gamma_2
payment. The same conclusion holds if capture means its buffered closed
halfspace instead of its smoothed boundary weight.

The exact menu, rho, covariance normalization, common budget, width A,
and source energy are all retained. The example does NOT assert that this
triangle is a global minimizer of the body-only smoothed objective. A
compensated inequality using the FULL stationary surface separator might
still use additional global information or the W/target terms. What (9)--
(13) exclude is recovering Gamma_d simply by turning the positive H-plus-
covariance part into a probability law and applying a cap theorem to it.

## 7. Status

Equations (1)--(6) are exact identities and a valid weaker payment.
The extra-degree facet theorem gives an existential escort center, not
the actual source-section center. Equations (9)--(13) are an actual
balanced common-budget obstruction to the proposed local normalized
compensation. They do not solve or disprove OC or the full stationary
mixed separator payment.
